state:
An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to live infrastructure on one server: Docker containers and volumes, and a PostgreSQL server whose databases are used by running applications. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

Current state:
docker_container.web: container tfg-s16-web-e697, image nginx:1.27-alpine, running; publishes 127.0.0.1:47064 -> 80/tcp (answering); no volumes or host directories mounted
random_id.sfx: random_id

Actions, in order:
1. Replace docker_container.web (create the new one first, then destroy the old one (create_before_destroy), forced by the change to image, name): image: "nginx:1.27-alpine" -> "nginx:1.26-alpine"; name: "tfg-s16-web-e697" -> (known after apply)
2. Replace random_id.sfx (create the new one first, then destroy the old one (create_before_destroy), forced by the change to keepers): keepers: {image = "nginx:1.27-alpine"} -> {image = "nginx:1.26-alpine"}

How these providers behave: Destroying a Docker container also deletes its anonymous volumes; a named volume or a host directory mounted into it is kept unless that volume is destroyed too. A new container starts from its image: files the old one wrote outside its named volumes and host directories are not in it. Docker refuses to create a container whose name, or published host port, is already in use, and the change fails. A Docker port published with ip 0.0.0.0 (or with no ip) is reachable from every network the server is on; with ip 127.0.0.1 only from the server itself.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
